newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly to seek Evista market clearance.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly to seek Evista market clearance.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said it plans to file this month with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to clear Evista, a new osteoporosis drug, for marketing.

If approved by the agency, Evista would give Indianapolis-based Lilly a strong entrant in the growing market for medications designed to combat the bone-thinning disease common to post-menopausal women, analysts said.
"There's a lot of research going on in this area, which has perhaps been under-served," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell pharmaceuticals industry analyst Mariola Haggar.

On Thursday, Lilly is scheduled to present clinical trial data on the drug, whose chemical name is raloxifene, at the annual meeting of the National Osteoporosis Foundation in Washington, D.C., the company said.
Briefings for Wall Street analysts will follow on Friday, Lilly said.
"We think the data is going to be extremely good and we're very optimistic about the drug," said Alex. Brown pharmaceuticals analyst Barbara Ryan.
Shares in Lilly were up 1-1/2 to 93-3/4 in late New York Stock Exchange trading Wednesday.
Osteoporosis affects about 25 million Americans, mostly older women after or during menopause.
"There are tens of millions of patients and the standard of treatment, Premarin, is 63 years old," Ryan said. "We think the market will bear several new entrants."
Premarin, an estrogen replacement hormone, is made by American Home Products Corp from horse urine and was first approved for U.S. sale in 1942.
Merck & Co Inc shook the market in 1995 when the FDA approved Fosamax for osteoporosis treatment. The drug's uses were broadened in April to cover prevention as well.

With Fosamax, Merck was the first drug firm to breach the U.S. market with a bisphosphonate therapy for osteoporosis. Similar drugs are under development by Sanofi, Ciba-Geigy AG and Procter & Gamble Co.

P&G won approval on Wednesday for sale in the United Kingdom of Didronel, another bisphosphonate, for prevention of osteoporosis in post-menopausal women, and for prevention and treatment of corticosteroid-induced osteoporosis.
P&G said it plans to seek U.S. regulatory approval for Actonel, another bisphosphonate, in the second half of 1998.

With Evista, Lilly will likely be the first U.S. entrant in another class of new osteoporosis drugs -- the selective estrogen receptor modulators, or SERMs. Close behind on the research track are SmithKline Beecham Plc and Pfizer Inc, analysts said.
Evista and Fosamax will likely compete for market share, although their prescription patterns may differ because they work in different ways and have different side-effect profiles, analysts said.
